title: Ladakh: Leh, Nubra, Pangong, Tso Moriri and Kargil
selection: VacayOut had no Ladakh pages. This pack adds the Ladakh page and its main destinations — Leh and the Indus monasteries, Nubra, Pangong Tso, Tso Moriri and Kargil — with itineraries and guides to altitude, permits and seasons, researched from Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism), the Leh district administration's tourist portal and Wikipedia.

LA1.claim: Ladakh is a high-altitude desert, often called 'Little Tibet', famous for its Buddhist monasteries.

evidence.quote: Ladakh unfolds as a breathtaking spectacle, a high-altitude desert
Renowned as "Little Tibet,"

LA2.claim: Ladakh opened to tourism in 1974, with only 527 visitors that year; tourism now earns over 60% of its revenue.

evidence.quote: Ladakh formally opened for tourism in 1974 with only 527 tourists visiting the region
The Tourism Industry accounts for more than 60% of the total revenue generated in Ladakh.

LA3.claim: Every visitor to Leh must spend at least 48 hours acclimatising before going higher; road travel does not help acclimatisation.

evidence.quote: All tourist/visitors arriving in Leh must undergo at least 48 hrs of acclimatization before initiating their journey to high altitude areas
Road travel does not help at all in acclimatization.

LA4.claim: HAPE and HACE can be fatal — see a doctor at once if symptoms appear; drink 2–3 litres of water a day and avoid alcohol and smoking.

evidence.quote: In case of symptoms of HAPE/HACE kindly consult a doctor immediately.
Tourists should have at least 2-3 ltrs. of water per day and should avoid alcohol, smoking cigarettes and sedatives

LA5.claim: Tourists pay a fee (environment/green fee, Red Cross fund and wildlife fee) online on the Leh permit portal; foreigners need a Protected Area Permit for Pangong, Nubra, Khardung La and Tso Moriri.

evidence.quote: The fee includes the environmental fee (green fee), Red Cross Fund and wildlife fee.
require protected area permit to visit protected/restricted areas (like pangong, nobra, khardongla, tsomoriri, etc.) of ladakh

LA6.claim: Leh's Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, at 3,256 m, is the highest commercial airport in India.

evidence.quote: Situated at 3,256 m (10,682 ft) above mean sea level, it is the highest commercial airport in India

LA7.claim: Leh is reached by road on the 434 km Srinagar–Leh highway and the Leh–Manali highway.

evidence.quote: The principal access roads include the 434 kilometres (270 mi) Srinagar -Leh highway

LA8.claim: The ideal time to visit is spring–summer, February to October; Leh's winters, late November to early March, are long and very cold.

evidence.quote: The ideal time to visit is during Spring-Summer February-October.
Leh has a cold desert climate ( Köppen climate classification BWk ) with long, cold winters from late November to early March

LA9.claim: Try thukpa, tsampa (ngamphe), skyu and momos; chang is the local celebratory drink.

evidence.quote: Delight in the heartwarming flavours of Thukpa, a soul-soothing noodle soup, and Tsampa, known locally as Ngamphe
Treat your palate to the hearty indulgence of Skyu

LH1.claim: Leh, Ladakh's main town at about 3,500 m on the Indus, was a hub of the caravan trade between Punjab, Central Asia, Kashmir and Tibet until 1949.

evidence.quote: Leh is at an altitude of 3,524 m (11,562 ft)
From the 17th century right until 1949, Ladakh’s principal town, Leh, was the hub of the bustling caravan trade between Punjab and Central Asia, and between Kashmir and Tibet.

LH2.claim: Most visitors get mild headaches and breathlessness at first; take it easy and avoid exertion on arrival.

evidence.quote: The altitude means that most visitors initially suffer mild headaches and breathlessness.

LH3.claim: Hemis festival (June/July), Sindhu Darshan (11–13 June), the Ladakh Festival (20–26 September) and the Thiksey festival (October/November).

evidence.quote: Hemis festival (Jun/Jul)
Sindhu darshan (11–13 Jun)
Ladakh festival (20–26 Sep)
Thiksey festival (Oct/Nov)

LHP1.claim: The nine-storey Leh Palace was built in the 1630s by King Sengge Namgyal, in the tradition of Lhasa's Potala, which it predates by about 50 years.

evidence.quote: The town is dominated by the nine-storeyed Leh Palace , built in the 1630s by Sengge Namgyal.
The palace’s massive inward - leaning walls are in the same architectural tradition as the Potala Palace in Lhasa which the Leh Palace antedates by about 50 years.

LHP2.claim: It has been unoccupied since 1846; carry a torch for the uneven floors. Tsemo Fort crowns the ridge above.

evidence.quote: Carry a flashlight and watch out for uneven floor.
the 16th-century Tsemo (Victory) Fort is a defining landmark that crowns the top of Palace Ridge.

LHS1.claim: The Shanti Stupa, built in 1991 and unveiled by the Dalai Lama, is reached by 500 steps; open 5 am–9 pm.

evidence.quote: The stupa was built in 1991 under the guidance of Bhikshu Gyomyo Nakamura
You need to climb 500 steps to reach this place

LHT1.claim: Thiksey, a twelve-storey Gelug monastery 19 km east of Leh, resembles the Potala Palace and has a Maitreya temple.

evidence.quote: It is located on top of a hill in Thiksey approximately 19 kilometres (12 mi) east of Leh
It is a twelve-storey complex and houses many items of Buddhist art
It is noted for its resemblance to the Potala Palace

LHH1.claim: Hemis, 45 km from Leh, is the largest and richest monastery of central Ladakh; its festival for Padmasambhava falls in June.

evidence.quote: Situated 45 km from Leh , it was re-established in 1672 by the Ladakhi king Sengge Namgyal . The annual Hemis festival honouring Padmasambhava is held there in early June.
Hemis is the largest as well as the richest of the central Ladakh monasteries.

LHH2.claim: Every 12 years it unveils a three-storey embroidered thangka of Padmasambhava; the last unveiling was in 2016.

evidence.quote: an enormous, three-storey high thangka of Padmasambhava, embroidered and studded with pearls and semi-precious stones. The last unveiling of the thangka was held in 2016.

LHK1.claim: Stok Palace has housed the Namgyal royal family since 1843; part is a museum with 35 thangkas of the Buddha's life.

evidence.quote: The palace at Stok has been the residence of the Namgyals, the former rulers of Ladakh, since its independence in 1843.
Its collections include a set of 35 thangkas representing the life of the Buddha

LHA1.claim: Alchi, founded in the early 12th century, has remarkably preserved 12th–13th-century murals, as it was abandoned for worship by the 16th century.

evidence.quote: Founded in the early 12th century AD, the religious enclave of Alchi is the jewel among Ladakh’s monasteries.
the 12th- and 13th-century paintings in its temples have remained remarkably well preserved

LHM1.claim: At Magnetic Hill, 30 km from Leh, an optical illusion makes a downhill slope look uphill, so cars in neutral seem to roll upward.

evidence.quote: Just 30 km from the charming town of Leh, the Magnetic Hill rests amidst the embrace of the Sindhu river
is actually an optical illusion, revealing itself to be a downhill slope.

LHG1.claim: Gurudwara Pathar Sahib, at 12,000 ft on the Leh–Nimu road, marks Guru Nanak's visit in 1517; open 6 am–7 pm.

evidence.quote: an iconic gurudwara situated at an altitude of 12,000 feet.
erected in 1517 to commemorate the visit of Sikh Guru Nanak Dev

LHL1.claim: Lamayuru (Yuru Gompa), about 127 km from Leh, is one of Ladakh's oldest monasteries, beside the 'Moonland' landscape.

evidence.quote: At about 127 kilometres from Leh town
It is one of the oldest and largest in Ladakh
Discover the otherworldly charm of MoonLand near Lamayuru on the Leh-Kargil Road

LHN1.claim: Hemis National Park, set up in 1981, covers about 4,400 sq km and protects snow leopards and Tibetan wolves.

evidence.quote: Established in 1981, it covers an area of about 4,400 square kilometres
including rare and endangered species like the Tibetan wolf, Snow

NB1.claim: The road from Leh to Diskit in Nubra, about 110 km and five hours, crosses Khardung La.

evidence.quote: The five-hour journey of some 110 kilometers from Leh to Diskit

NB2.claim: Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit to visit Nubra.

evidence.quote: Foreign nationals are required to get a Protected area permit to visit Nubra.

NBK1.claim: Khardung La, 40 km north of Leh at about 5,359 m, is one of the world's highest motorable roads.

evidence.quote: Khardung Pass (elevation 5,359 m (17,582 ft) )
40 km (25 mi) north of Leh city
The road is one of the world's highest motorable roads.

NBD1.claim: Diskit, founded in the 15th century, is the oldest and largest monastery in Nubra, with a giant Maitreya Buddha unveiled by the Dalai Lama in 2010.

evidence.quote: Diskit Monastery is the largest and oldest Buddhist monastery in the valley.
The giant statue was inaugurated by the Dalai Lama in 2010
Opening time - 07:00 AM to 01:00 PM and 02:00 PM to 07:00 PM

NBH1.claim: Hunder, about 10 km from Diskit, has sand dunes and double-humped Bactrian camels.

evidence.quote: as one enters Hunder, some 10 kilometers from Diskit.
explore the stunning dunes of Hunder on rare, double-humped Bactrian camels.

NBT1.claim: Turtuk, a Balti village about 90 km beyond Diskit on the Shyok, was under Pakistani control until 1971; it is famous for apricot orchards.

evidence.quote: From Diskit or Hunder, a 90 km gorgeous ride
Turtuk was administered by Pakistan and was under Pakistani control until the war of 1971
amble through its famed apricot orchards and barley fields.

PG1.claim: Pangong Tso, at about 4,300 m, stretches 134 km into Tibet; about two-thirds lies in Chinese-administered territory.

evidence.quote: It stretches for 134 km (83 mi) and is 5 km (3.1 mi) wide at its broadest point.
Approximately two-thirds of the lake lies within the area administered by China

PG2.claim: Despite its salinity the lake freezes in winter.

evidence.quote: Despite its high salinity, the lake freezes in the winter.

PG3.claim: The road to Pangong crosses Chang La at about 5,360 m.

evidence.quote: Chang La is a high mountain pass in Ladakh at an elevation of 5,360 m (17,590 ft)
The Chang La, on Leh to Pangong Lake road

TM1.claim: Tso Moriri, a Ramsar wetland at about 4,600 m in the Rupshu valley, is a breeding ground for black-necked cranes; Korzok's barley fields are among the highest cultivated land in the world.

evidence.quote: It is officially known as Tso Moriri Wetland Conservation Reserve and is a wetland reserve under the Ramsar site.
Tso Moriri is at an altitude of 4,600 m (15,092ft)
breeding areas for many species of migratory birds, such as the rare black-necked crane

TM2.claim: Pangong and Tso Moriri are reached by road, but there are no scheduled buses.

evidence.quote: are accessible by road, although there are no scheduled bus services.

KG1.claim: Dras, the 'Gateway to Ladakh', is called the second coldest inhabited place on Earth.

evidence.quote: a journey to Dras - the second coldest inhabited place on Earth - awaits. Known as ‘The Gateway to Ladakh,’

KGW1.claim: The Kargil War Memorial at Dras, 60 km from Kargil, honours those who died in the 1999 war; Kargil Vijay Diwas is on 26 July.

evidence.quote: This beautiful memorial is in Dras, 60 km from Kargil.
Every year on 26th July, Kargil Vijay Diwas is observed here
Opening time - 10:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 02:00 PM - 05:00 PM

KGM1.claim: Mulbekh has a 30-foot rock-carved Maitreya Buddha beside the old Ladakh–Kashmir trade route.

evidence.quote: Visit the Mulbekh Monastery, where an impressive 30-foot Maitreya Buddha statue stands proudly.
overlooks the ancient trade route between Ladakh and Kashmir

LA_112.claim: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

evidence.quote: 112 is now the pan-country single emergency number for all emergencies.

LA_VISA.claim: e-Tourist visa applications should be made at least 4 days before arrival, with a passport valid for at least six months.

evidence.quote: For e-Tourist and e-Business visa, Applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival.
Applicant's passport should have at least six months validity at the time of making application for grant of e-Visa.

LA_UPI.claim: International visitors can pay by QR code using NPCI's UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa KYC check.

evidence.quote: The UPI One World wallet can be availed through authorized PPI issuers at airports, hotels, designated money exchange locations and other touchpoints, following a full KYC process based on a passport and valid visa.

overview.text:
Ladakh is a high-altitude desert often called 'Little Tibet'. It opened to tourism only in 1974, when 527 visitors came; today tourism is its biggest earner.

Leh is the base, with its palace and the great monasteries of the Indus valley — Thiksey, Hemis and Alchi. Over Khardung La lies the Nubra Valley with its dunes and Bactrian camels; to the east are the high lakes of Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri, and to the west Kargil and Dras.

items.body: Leh Palace and the Shanti Stupa.
Thiksey and Hemis monasteries.
Khardung La and the Nubra Valley.
Pangong Tso.
Tso Moriri's cranes.
The Kargil War Memorial.

how_to_reach.text: Fly into Leh's Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, at 3,256 m the highest commercial airport in India. By road, Leh is on the 434 km Srinagar–Leh highway and the Leh–Manali highway.

best_time.text: Spring to summer, February to October, is the ideal time. Leh's winters, from late November to early March, are long and very cold.

items.title: Acclimatise
items.body: Spend at least 48 hours in Leh before going higher — road travel does not help acclimatisation.

items.title: Know the warning signs
items.body: HAPE and HACE can be fatal: see a doctor at once if symptoms appear.

items.title: Look after yourself
items.body: Drink 2–3 litres of water a day and avoid alcohol and smoking.

items.title: Visas
items.body: Apply for an e-Tourist visa at least 4 days before arrival; your passport needs at least six months' validity.

items.title: Payments
items.body: Visitors can pay by QR code with NPCI's UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa KYC check. Carry some cash for small purchases.

items.title: Emergency
items.body: Dial 112 for police, fire or ambulance.

items.title: Permits and fees
items.body: Pay the tourist fee (green fee, Red Cross fund, wildlife fee) online on the Leh permit portal. Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit for Pangong, Nubra, Khardung La and Tso Moriri.
Thukpa, tsampa (ngamphe), skyu and momos.
Chang, the local barley drink, for celebrations.

items.body: Tourists pay a fee on the Leh permit portal; foreigners need a Protected Area Permit for Pangong, Nubra, Khardung La and Tso Moriri.

items.body: At least 48 hours in Leh before going higher.

items.title: When is the best time to visit?
items.body: February to October.

overview.text:
Leh sits at about 3,500 m on the Indus. Until 1949 it was a hub of the caravan trade between Punjab, Central Asia, Kashmir and Tibet. Above the old town rise the nine-storey Leh Palace and Tsemo Fort; the Shanti Stupa looks across from the other side.

Around Leh are the great monasteries — Thiksey, Hemis, Alchi — Stok Palace, Magnetic Hill and Gurudwara Pathar Sahib.

how_to_reach.text: Leh's airport, at 3,256 m, is the highest commercial airport in India. By road, take the Srinagar–Leh or Leh–Manali highway.

best_time.text: Festivals: Hemis (June/July), Sindhu Darshan (11–13 June), the Ladakh Festival (20–26 September) and Thiksey (October/November).

items.title: First days
items.body: Most visitors feel mild headaches and breathlessness at first — rest, and spend at least 48 hours in Leh before going higher.
Leh Palace: The nine-storey Leh Palace was built in the 1630s by King Sengge Namgyal, in the tradition of Lhasa's Potala, which it predates by about 50 years.
Shanti Stupa: The Shanti Stupa, built in 1991 and unveiled by the Dalai Lama, is reached by 500 steps; open 5 am–9 pm.
Thiksey Monastery: Thiksey, a twelve-storey Gelug monastery 19 km east of Leh, resembles the Potala Palace and has a Maitreya temple.
Hemis Monastery: Hemis, 45 km from Leh, is the largest and richest monastery of central Ladakh; its festival for Padmasambhava falls in June.
Stok Palace: Stok Palace has housed the Namgyal royal family since 1843; part is a museum with 35 thangkas of the Buddha's life.

overview.text: The drive from Leh to Diskit, about 110 km and five hours, crosses Khardung La. Nubra's highlights are the Diskit Monastery and its giant Buddha, the sand dunes and Bactrian camels of Hunder, and Turtuk, a Balti village 90 km further on.

items.title: Permit
items.body: Foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit for Nubra.
Khardung La: Khardung La, 40 km north of Leh at about 5,359 m, is one of the world's highest motorable roads.
Diskit Monastery: Diskit, founded in the 15th century, is the oldest and largest monastery in Nubra, with a giant Maitreya Buddha unveiled by the Dalai Lama in 2010.
Hunder Sand Dunes: Hunder, about 10 km from Diskit, has sand dunes and double-humped Bactrian camels.
Turtuk: Turtuk, a Balti village about 90 km beyond Diskit on the Shyok, was under Pakistani control until 1971; it is famous for apricot orchards.

guides.title: Ladakh altitude guide: acclimatisation and safety
guides.summary: The official advice on acclimatising in Leh, warning signs, and how to plan your first days.
guides.seoDescription: Ladakh altitude safety: 48 hours' acclimatisation in Leh, why road travel doesn't help, HAPE/HACE warning signs, water and alcohol.

body.intro: Leh is at about 3,500 m and the passes go far higher. Plan your first days around the altitude.

sections.heading: The 48-hour rule
sections.text: The Leh administration asks every visitor to spend at least 48 hours in Leh before going to higher areas. Arriving by road does not help acclimatisation.

sections.heading: First days
sections.text: Most visitors feel mild headaches and breathlessness at first. Rest, and avoid exertion.

sections.heading: Look after yourself
sections.text: Drink 2–3 litres of water a day and avoid alcohol, smoking and sedatives.

sections.heading: Warning signs
sections.text: HAPE and HACE can be fatal. If symptoms appear, see a doctor immediately.

guides.title: Ladakh permits and fees: what you need
guides.summary: The tourist fee, protected-area permits for foreigners, and Nubra, Pangong, Khardung La and Tso Moriri.
guides.seoTitle: Ladakh Permits & Fees: Nubra, Pangong, Tso Moriri
guides.seoDescription: Ladakh permits: the tourist fee paid online, and Protected Area Permits for foreigners visiting Nubra, Pangong, Khardung La and Tso Moriri.

body.intro: A little paperwork before you go saves a lot of hassle.

sections.heading: Tourist fee
sections.text: Visitors pay a fee — environment (green) fee, Red Cross fund and wildlife fee — online on the Leh District Tourists Management System.

sections.heading: Foreign nationals
sections.text: Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit for protected areas such as Pangong, Nubra, Khardung La and Tso Moriri.

sections.heading: Getting around
sections.text: Pangong and Tso Moriri are reached by road only; there are no scheduled buses.

guides.title: Best time to visit Ladakh
guides.summary: When to go, festival dates, and what winter is like.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Ladakh: Seasons & Festivals
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Ladakh: February–October, Hemis in June, Sindhu Darshan, the Ladakh Festival in September, and Leh's long cold winters.

body.intro: Ladakh's season is set by its altitude and its long, cold winters.

sections.heading: Season
sections.text: Spring to summer, February to October, is the ideal time. Leh's winters, late November to early March, are long and very cold.
